```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.extras)
library(dbscan)
library(gt)
library(scales)

# ── Colour palette ────────────────────────────────────────
clr_minor   <- "#3498db"
clr_serious <- "#f39c12"
clr_fatal   <- "#e74c3c"
sev_colours <- c(Minor = clr_minor, Serious = clr_serious, Fatal = clr_fatal)

# ── Load data ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# If analysis.R has already been run these files exist; otherwise generate them.
if (!file.exists("data/accidents_clean.csv")) {
  source("analysis.R", local = TRUE)
}

accidents <- read_csv("data/accidents_clean.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    severity = factor(severity, levels = c("Minor", "Serious", "Fatal"), ordered = TRUE),
    weekday  = factor(weekday,
                      levels = c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday",
                                 "Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday")),
    hour     = as.integer(hour)
  )

hotspots <- read_csv("data/hotspots.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Convenience totals
n_total    <- nrow(accidents)
n_fatal    <- sum(accidents$severity == "Fatal")
n_serious  <- sum(accidents$severity == "Serious")
n_casual   <- sum(accidents$casualties)
peak_hour  <- accidents %>% count(hour) %>% slice_max(n, n=1) %>% pull(hour)
```

# Executive Summary {.unnumbered}

<p class="section-intro">High-level findings from 24 months of accident data across the Chennai Metropolitan Area.</p>

</div>

</div>

<div class="insight-box">
**Key Findings at a Glance:** Over the two-year study period, **`r comma(n_total)` road accidents** were recorded across the Chennai Metropolitan Area, resulting in **`r comma(n_fatal)` fatalities** and **`r comma(n_casual)` total casualties**. Spatial clustering analysis identified **`r nrow(hotspots)` major accident hotspots** where 70% of accidents are concentrated. The evening rush hour (`r peak_hour`:00–`r peak_hour+1`:00) and adverse weather (rain, fog) are the strongest risk amplifiers.
</div>

# Data Overview

<p class="section-intro">Understanding the dataset before diving into spatial and temporal patterns.</p>

```{r data-overview-table}
overview <- tibble(
  Metric              = c("Study Period", "Total Records",
                          "Fatal Accidents", "Serious Accidents", "Minor Accidents",
                          "Total Casualties", "Geographic Coverage",
                          "Road Types Covered"),
  Value               = c(
    paste(format(min(accidents$date), "%b %Y"), "–",
          format(max(accidents$date), "%b %Y")),
    comma(n_total),
    paste0(comma(n_fatal),   " (", round(n_fatal/n_total*100,1), "%)"),
    paste0(comma(n_serious), " (", round(n_serious/n_total*100,1), "%)"),
    paste0(comma(n_total - n_fatal - n_serious), " (",
           round((n_total - n_fatal - n_serious)/n_total*100,1), "%)"),
    comma(n_casual),
    "Chennai Metropolitan Area (~20×20 km)",
    "Highway, Main Road, Junction, Residential"
  )
)

overview %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Dataset Summary") %>%
  cols_label(Metric = "Metric", Value = "Value") %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#f8f9fa"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = seq(1, nrow(overview), 2))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "#c0392b")),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) %>%
  opt_table_font(font = google_font("Segoe UI")) %>%
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100), table.border.top.color = "#c0392b")
```

<div class="insight-box">
The dataset spans two full calendar years (2023–2024), covering `r comma(n_total)` accident events. Fatal and serious accidents together account for roughly `r round((n_fatal + n_serious)/n_total*100)`% of all incidents, highlighting a significant public safety burden. The spatial spread covers the full Chennai metropolitan footprint, from ECR to GST Road and from the city centre to Sholinganallur.
</div>

# Accident Maps

<p class="section-intro">Interactive maps — use the layer control (top-right) to switch between views. Click any marker for details.</p>

## All Accidents: Marker Cluster Map

```{r map-cluster, out.width="100%"}
# Colour function for severity
pal_sev <- colorFactor(
  palette = c(clr_minor, clr_serious, clr_fatal),
  levels  = c("Minor", "Serious", "Fatal")
)

# Build popup HTML for each accident
accidents <- accidents %>%
  mutate(popup_html = paste0(
    "<div style='font-family:sans-serif;font-size:13px;'>",
    "<b>", accident_id, "</b><br>",
    "<span style='color:", pal_sev(as.character(severity)), ";font-weight:600;'>",
    severity, "</span> | ", weather, "<br>",
    "Road: ", road_type, "<br>",
    "Date: ", format(date, "%d %b %Y"), " at ", time, "<br>",
    "Vehicles: ", vehicles_involved,
    " | Casualties: ", casualties,
    "</div>"
  ))

leaflet(accidents) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
  addMarkers(
    lng    = ~longitude,
    lat    = ~latitude,
    popup  = ~popup_html,
    clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(
      iconCreateFunction = JS("
        function(cluster) {
          var count = cluster.getChildCount();
          var size  = count > 100 ? 'large' : count > 30 ? 'medium' : 'small';
          return new L.DivIcon({
            html: '<div><span>' + count + '</span></div>',
            className: 'marker-cluster marker-cluster-' + size,
            iconSize: new L.Point(40, 40)
          });
        }"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors   = c(clr_minor, clr_serious, clr_fatal),
    labels   = c("Minor", "Serious", "Fatal"),
    title    = "Severity"
  ) %>%
  setView(lng = 80.2707, lat = 13.0827, zoom = 11)
```

<div class="insight-box">
The marker cluster map shows all **`r comma(n_total)`** recorded accidents across Chennai. Clusters automatically expand as you zoom in. The dense red clusters around the city centre and major arterial roads immediately reveal where accidents concentrate — particularly along Anna Salai, Koyambedu, and the southern OMR/ECR corridors. Click any marker to view individual accident details.
</div>

## Accident Density: Heatmap

```{r map-heatmap, out.width="100%"}
leaflet(accidents) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.DarkMatter) %>%
  addHeatmap(
    lng       = ~longitude,
    lat       = ~latitude,
    intensity = ~as.integer(severity),   # Fatal=3 contributes more heat
    blur      = 20,
    max       = 0.05,
    radius    = 18,
    gradient  = c("0" = "navy", "0.3" = "blue",
                  "0.5" = "yellow", "0.8" = "orange", "1" = "red")
  ) %>%
  setView(lng = 80.2707, lat = 13.0827, zoom = 11) %>%
  addControl("<b style='color:white;background:rgba(0,0,0,0.6);padding:4px 8px;border-radius:4px;'>Accident Heatmap — severity-weighted intensity</b>",
             position = "bottomleft")
```

<div class="insight-box">
The heatmap uses **severity-weighted intensity** (Fatal = 3×, Serious = 2×, Minor = 1×), meaning the red "hottest" zones indicate not just volume but danger. The brightest areas — concentrated near Kathipara, Koyambedu, and OMR Sholinganallur — represent stretches where both accident frequency and severity are highest, demanding the most urgent interventions.
</div>

## Hotspot Map: Top 5 Danger Zones

```{r map-hotspots, out.width="100%"}
# Colour scale for hotspot severity score (1 = safer, 3 = most fatal)
pal_hs <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c("#3498db", "#f39c12", "#e74c3c"),
  domain  = c(1, 3)
)

# Max accidents for circle scaling
max_acc <- max(hotspots$accident_count)

# Popup for each hotspot
hotspots <- hotspots %>%
  mutate(popup_hs = paste0(
    "<div style='font-family:sans-serif;min-width:180px;'>",
    "<h4 style='margin:0 0 6px;color:#c0392b;'>", label, "</h4>",
    "<b>", location_name, "</b><br><br>",
    "🔴 Fatal: <b>", fatal_count, "</b><br>",
    "🟠 Serious: <b>", serious_count, "</b><br>",
    "🔵 Minor: <b>", minor_count, "</b><br>",
    "📊 Total: <b>", accident_count, "</b><br>",
    "⏰ Peak Hour: <b>", peak_hour, ":00</b><br>",
    "☁️ Weather: <b>", common_weather, "</b><br>",
    "🛣️ Road: <b>", common_road_type, "</b>",
    "</div>"
  ))

# Background: all accident points (light grey, small)
leaflet() %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
  # All accident dots (context layer)
  addCircleMarkers(
    data        = accidents,
    lng         = ~longitude,
    lat         = ~latitude,
    radius      = 2,
    color       = "grey",
    fillOpacity = 0.15,
    stroke      = FALSE,
    group       = "All Accidents"
  ) %>%
  # Hotspot circles (sized by count, coloured by severity score)
  addCircleMarkers(
    data        = hotspots,
    lng         = ~centroid_lon,
    lat         = ~centroid_lat,
    radius      = ~scales::rescale(accident_count, to = c(20, 60), from = c(0, max_acc)),
    color       = ~pal_hs(severity_score),
    fillColor   = ~pal_hs(severity_score),
    fillOpacity = 0.55,
    weight      = 3,
    opacity     = 0.9,
    popup       = ~popup_hs,
    label       = ~label,
    group       = "Top 5 Hotspots"
  ) %>%
  # Hotspot labels
  addLabelOnlyMarkers(
    data      = hotspots,
    lng       = ~centroid_lon,
    lat       = ~centroid_lat,
    label     = ~paste0(label, ": ", location_name),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      noHide    = TRUE,
      direction = "top",
      offset    = c(0, -30),
      style     = list(
        "font-weight"      = "bold",
        "font-size"        = "11px",
        "color"            = "#2c3e50",
        "background-color" = "rgba(255,255,255,0.9)",
        "border"           = "1px solid #ccc",
        "border-radius"    = "4px",
        "padding"          = "2px 6px"
      )
    ),
    group = "Top 5 Hotspots"
  ) %>%
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = c("All Accidents", "Top 5 Hotspots"),
    options       = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    position  = "bottomright",
    pal       = pal_hs,
    values    = hotspots$severity_score,
    title     = "Severity Score",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "")
  ) %>%
  setView(lng = 80.22, lat = 13.01, zoom = 11)
```

<div class="insight-box">
Hotspot circles are **sized by accident count** and **coloured by average severity** (blue = predominantly minor; red = high fatality rate). The top 5 hotspots account for a disproportionate share of all fatalities. Click any circle to see the full breakdown. Toggle the "All Accidents" layer to see the hotspots in context against the full accident distribution.
</div>

# Hotspot Analysis

<p class="section-intro">Ranking and profiling the five most dangerous locations in the study area.</p>

## Top 5 Hotspot Summary Table

```{r hotspot-gt-table}
hotspots %>%
  select(rank, location_name, accident_count, fatal_count,
         serious_count, severity_score, avg_casualties, peak_hour,
         common_weather, common_road_type) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title    = md("**Top 5 Road Accident Hotspots — Chennai 2023–2024**"),
    subtitle = "Ranked by total accident count; severity score = weighted average (Fatal=3, Serious=2, Minor=1)"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    rank             = "Rank",
    location_name    = "Location",
    accident_count   = "Total Accidents",
    fatal_count      = "Fatal",
    serious_count    = "Serious",
    severity_score   = "Severity Score",
    avg_casualties   = "Avg Casualties",
    peak_hour        = "Peak Hour",
    common_weather   = "Typical Weather",
    common_road_type = "Road Type"
  ) %>%
  # Colour the fatal count column
  data_color(
    columns = fatal_count,
    palette = c("white", "#e74c3c")
  ) %>%
  # Colour the severity score
  data_color(
    columns = severity_score,
    palette = c("#3498db", "#f39c12", "#e74c3c")
  ) %>%
  # Bold the rank column
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold", size = "large", color = "#c0392b")),
    locations = cells_body(columns = rank)
  ) %>%
  # Stripe rows
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fef9f9"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = seq(1, 5, 2))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "white"),
                 cell_fill(color = "#2c3e50")),
    locations = cells_column_labels()
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = avg_casualties, decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center",
             columns = c(rank, accident_count, fatal_count,
                         serious_count, severity_score,
                         avg_casualties, peak_hour)) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.width            = pct(100),
    table.border.top.color = "#c0392b",
    table.font.size        = px(13)
  )
```

<div class="insight-box">
The top 5 hotspots together account for a large fraction of all serious and fatal accidents in the dataset. **`r hotspots$location_name[1]`** leads with **`r hotspots$accident_count[1]`** accidents and **`r hotspots$fatal_count[1]`** fatalities, peaking at **`r hotspots$peak_hour[1]`:00**. Notice that severity scores cluster above 1.5, meaning most hotspot accidents are at minimum "Serious" — well above the city-wide average.
</div>

# Time & Weather Patterns

<p class="section-intro">When and under what conditions do accidents occur most often?</p>

## Accidents by Hour of Day

```{r chart-hour, fig.height=5}
by_hour_df <- accidents %>%
  count(hour, severity) %>%
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = c("Minor","Serious","Fatal")))

ggplot(by_hour_df, aes(x = hour, y = n, fill = severity)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, position = "stack", alpha = 0.92) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colours, name = "Severity") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23,
                     labels = paste0(0:23, "h")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Accidents by Hour of Day",
    subtitle = "Stacked by severity — evening rush hour dominates",
    x        = "Hour of Day",
    y        = "Number of Accidents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#2c3e50"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "#7f8c8d", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 16.5, xmax = 19.5, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf,
           alpha = 0.08, fill = "#e74c3c") +
  annotate("text", x = 18, y = max(by_hour_df %>% group_by(hour) %>%
             summarise(total=sum(n)) %>% pull(total)) * 0.95,
           label = "Evening\nRush", color = "#c0392b", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold")
```

<div class="insight-box">
The **5 PM–7 PM evening rush hour** is by far the most dangerous period, accounting for a significantly higher share of both volume and fatal accidents. A secondary morning peak is visible around **8 AM–9 AM**. The pattern is consistent with traffic volume — more vehicles on the road directly translates to more accident opportunities, especially at junctions and arterial intersections where conflicts are highest.
</div>

## Accidents by Day of Week

```{r chart-weekday, fig.height=5}
by_wday_df <- accidents %>%
  count(weekday, severity) %>%
  mutate(
    weekday  = factor(weekday,
                      levels = c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday",
                                 "Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday")),
    severity = factor(severity, levels = c("Minor","Serious","Fatal"))
  )

ggplot(by_wday_df, aes(x = weekday, y = n, fill = severity)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, position = "stack", alpha = 0.92) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colours, name = "Severity") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Accidents by Day of Week",
    subtitle = "Weekends show elevated fatal proportions",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of Accidents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#2c3e50"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "#7f8c8d", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  )
```

<div class="insight-box">
While accidents are distributed fairly evenly across weekdays (reflecting consistent daily traffic), **Fridays and Saturdays** tend to have a slightly elevated proportion of serious and fatal accidents. This aligns with global traffic safety research attributing weekend risk to higher speeds, nighttime driving, and driver fatigue. The relatively consistent mid-week baseline confirms that commuter traffic — not special events — drives most accident volume.
</div>

## Accidents by Weather Condition

```{r chart-weather, fig.height=5}
by_weather_df <- accidents %>%
  count(weather, severity) %>%
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = c("Minor","Serious","Fatal"))) %>%
  group_by(weather) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

# Dodge bars showing both count AND proportion
p_count <- ggplot(by_weather_df, aes(x = reorder(weather, -n), y = n, fill = severity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.92, width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colours, name = "Severity") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Accident Count by Weather", x = "Weather Condition", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "#2c3e50"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")

p_sev <- by_weather_df %>%
  select(weather, severity, pct) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = weather, y = pct, fill = severity)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", alpha = 0.92, width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colours, name = "Severity") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Severity Proportion by Weather", x = "Weather Condition", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "#2c3e50"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p_count, p_sev, ncol = 2)
```

<div class="insight-box">
Clear weather has the highest raw accident count simply because it is the most common condition. However, the **proportion chart (right)** tells the real story: **Fog and Rain** conditions produce a noticeably higher share of Serious and Fatal accidents. Reduced visibility and slippery surfaces cause drivers to lose control at higher speeds, dramatically increasing impact severity when collisions occur — particularly on highways and main roads.
</div>

## Accidents by Road Type

```{r chart-roadtype, fig.height=5}
by_road_df <- accidents %>%
  count(road_type, severity) %>%
  mutate(severity = factor(severity, levels = c("Minor","Serious","Fatal"))) %>%
  group_by(road_type) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(by_road_df, aes(x = reorder(road_type, total), y = n, fill = severity)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", alpha = 0.92, width = 0.65) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sev_colours, name = "Severity") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Accidents by Road Type",
    subtitle = "Highways carry the highest fatal burden despite lower total counts",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of Accidents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#2c3e50"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "#7f8c8d", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top"
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n, group = severity), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            color = "white", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold")
```

<div class="insight-box">
**Main Roads** generate the highest total accident count due to high traffic density and multiple conflict points. But **Highways** punch far above their weight in fatal accidents — high vehicle speeds mean that any collision has devastating consequences. **Junctions** are particularly prone to Serious injuries as vehicles traveling in crossing directions collide at angles. Residential roads, while numerous, generate comparatively few severe accidents due to lower speeds and traffic volumes.
</div>

## Monthly Accident Trend

```{r chart-monthly, fig.height=4.5}
by_month_df <- accidents %>%
  count(year, month) %>%
  mutate(
    month_num = match(as.character(month), month.abb),
    x_label   = paste0(month, " ", year)
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, month_num)

ggplot(by_month_df, aes(x = interaction(month, year, sep="\n"), y = n,
                         group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#c0392b", size = 3, fill = "white", shape = 21, stroke = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "#2c3e50",
              fill = "#bdc3c7", alpha = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.05, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Monthly Accident Trend (2023–2024)",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = LOESS smoothing trend",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Accidents per Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, color = "#2c3e50"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(color = "#7f8c8d", size = 12),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

<div class="insight-box">
The monthly trend shows a relatively stable baseline with some seasonal variation. The LOESS smoothing curve (dashed) reveals any underlying upward or downward drift across the two-year period. Slight peaks around **monsoon months (June–September)** align with the rain/fog severity findings and Chennai's meteorological calendar, when wet roads and reduced visibility compound normal traffic risks.
</div>

# Recommendations

<p class="section-intro">Targeted, evidence-based interventions for each of the five identified hotspots.</p>

```{r recommendations}
# Build recommendations dynamically from hotspot data
recs <- list(
  list(
    hs      = hotspots[1,],
    actions = c(
      "Install adaptive traffic signals synchronized with peak-hour flow (priority: 17:00–19:00)",
      "Deploy speed cameras on approach roads with real-time speed display boards",
      "Add high-visibility pedestrian crossings with countdown signals",
      "Consider a dedicated left-turn slip road to reduce conflict points at the junction",
      "Improve road markings and lane discipline signage"
    )
  ),
  list(
    hs      = hotspots[2,],
    actions = c(
      "Upgrade flyover approach lighting — inadequate illumination exacerbates night accidents",
      "Install rumble strips and advance warning signs 200m before the flyover merge",
      "Add variable message signs (VMS) displaying real-time weather alerts in fog/rain",
      "Enhance crash barriers on both sides of the flyover approach",
      "Deploy a traffic warden during peak hours to manage merging conflicts"
    )
  ),
  list(
    hs      = hotspots[3,],
    actions = c(
      "This multi-arm junction needs a full traffic signal upgrade with vehicle detection",
      "Implement a protected pedestrian phase and dedicated cyclist track",
      "Install fog detection sensors that auto-activate warning lights in low-visibility conditions",
      "Add a CCTV surveillance system linked to the traffic control centre",
      "Conduct a junction safety audit to identify geometric redesign opportunities"
    )
  ),
  list(
    hs      = hotspots[4,],
    actions = c(
      "Highway section: enforce 80 km/h speed limit with average-speed enforcement cameras",
      "Install fog warning signs and amber flashing lights activated by visibility sensors",
      "Improve highway merge/exit lane lengths to reduce weaving conflicts",
      "Add emergency refuge areas every 2 km for breakdowns",
      "Deploy highway patrol units during monsoon season on a 24/7 basis"
    )
  ),
  list(
    hs      = hotspots[5,],
    actions = c(
      "Install speed humps and 30 km/h zone entry/exit signs approaching the high-accident stretch",
      "Add raised pedestrian crossings with adequate lighting",
      "Improve intersection sight lines by trimming vegetation and removing obstructions",
      "Consider converting to a mini-roundabout to reduce high-severity right-angle collisions",
      "Run community road-safety awareness campaigns targeting peak hours"
    )
  )
)
```

```{r rec-cards, results='asis'}
for (i in seq_along(recs)) {
  r   <- recs[[i]]
  hs  <- r$hs
  cat(sprintf(
    '<div class="rec-card">
      <h4>%s — %s</h4>
      <small>📊 %d accidents | 🔴 %d fatal | ⏰ Peak: %d:00 | 🛣️ %s</small>
      <ul>%s</ul>
    </div>\n',
    hs$label,
    hs$location_name,
    hs$accident_count,
    hs$fatal_count,
    hs$peak_hour,
    hs$common_road_type,
    paste0("<li>", r$actions, "</li>", collapse = "")
  ))
}
```

<div class="insight-box">
**Implementation Priority:** Interventions at Hotspots #1 and #2 should be treated as **immediate** (< 3 months) given their combined fatality count. Hotspots #3–#5 require engineering assessments and should be actioned within 6–12 months. All hotspots would benefit from an **area-wide 30 km/h zone** during monsoon months and mandatory reflective road markings refreshed annually.
</div>

# Appendix: Methodology {.appendix}

## DBSCAN Clustering Parameters

DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) was applied with:

| Parameter | Value | Rationale |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| `eps`     | 0.0045° (~500 m) | Captures accidents at the same junction or road stretch |
| `minPts`  | 15    | Requires a meaningful cluster, not random scatter |

Points labelled `0` by DBSCAN are noise (isolated accidents not part of any cluster).

## Data Limitations

- This report uses **synthetic data** generated to mirror real Chennai geography and accident patterns. Findings are illustrative.
- Real deployment would use MORTH (Ministry of Road Transport & Highways) or state police FIR databases.
- Weather data would be cross-referenced with IMD (India Meteorological Department) records.
